niche: online spiritual and shadow work courses
prompt_text: What are the best online courses for learning shadow work and spiritual practice?
answer_verbatim:
“Best” depends on whether you want a psychologically grounded approach, a specific spiritual tradition, or a mix. These are good places to start:

### Shadow work
- **[Engage the Shadow — Jung Platform](https://jungplatform.com/course/engage-the-shadow)** — A focused, Jungian-oriented course with video and audio lessons and practical exercises. A strong pick if you want structured exploration of shadow concepts rather than a general self-help course.
- **[Jung Platform’s shadow courses](https://jungplatform.com/program/shadow-courses)** — A broader learning path with several courses and talks from Jungian teachers. Better if you want to compare perspectives and go deeper over time.

### Spiritual practice
- **[Naropa University’s online learning courses](https://www.naropa.edu/academics/personal-enrichment/)** — Includes a free introductory mindfulness course connecting contemporary mindfulness with Buddhist traditions, plus longer contemplative offerings.
- **[Mindworks meditation courses](https://mindworks.org/meditation-courses/)** — Short, structured courses that pair daily study with meditation practice. A practical option if you want a regular routine and Buddhist-informed instruction.
- **[Tara Brach’s online courses](https://www.tarabrach.com/online-courses/)** — A good fit for mindfulness, compassion, and self-acceptance practices, especially if you like guided reflection and meditation.
- **[World Community for Christian Meditation courses](https://wccm.org/courses/)** — Worth considering if you want contemplative practice rooted in Christian spirituality.

**A sensible combination:** start with a short mindfulness course to build a steady, grounding practice, then add a shadow-work course if you want to explore recurring reactions, shame, or disowned parts of yourself. Shadow work can bring up difficult feelings, so go slowly, skip exercises that feel overwhelming, and consider working with a qualified therapist if it stirs up trauma or significant distress. Check each provider’s current schedule and fees before enrolling.
